subject: MediSphere DPA: redlines, SCCs and transfer impact - negotiation plan
messages:
From: Julia Harris <julia.harris@medisphere.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@medisphere.com
Date: 2028-03-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft DPA redlines for MediSphere — please review

Hi Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks again for the call last week. Attached is our initial set of DPA redlines (MediSphere_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx) and a short note from our privacy team describing the key asks. High-level items we want to confirm:

- Controller/processor mapping for the hosted inference paths (we're seeing mixed language between Order Form and DPA).
- Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) applicability for EU data and whether Redwood will propose a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) addendum.
- Any changes to subprocessor notification timelines (we're aiming for 30 days).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can accept the SCCs with the redline in section 7, or if you need to propose alternative language? We would prefer to have legal alignment by COB Mar 30 so we can get the Order Form finalized.

Attachment: MediSphere_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx (document, 842 KB)

Appreciate a quick read — happy to hop on a short call.

Best,
Julia Harris

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-03-28T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines for MediSphere — please review

Julia — thanks for sending, received and starting review. High level notes from my first pass:

- We agree in principle with SCCs but need to confirm whether the Order Form's hosting region language is aligned (EU-only vs multi-region). If MediSphere will require strict EU-only hosting for production data, that will change the routing controls and might require an operational addendum.
- Section 7 redline: we have a few technical/ops clarifications to propose instead of the deletions — I'll loop Ben for the precise substitute language.
- Subprocessor notification: we typically do 30 days for major changes and aim for notification within 14 days for security-critical subprocessors; we can propose a compromise clause.

I've attached a short note with inline comments for legal (KM_comments_DPA.pdf). Proposed next steps:
1) Internal alignment by EOD 3/29 (Legal + Privacy + Contracts).
2) Send a consolidated counter-redline to MediSphere by 3/29 evening (if possible).
3) Joint call 3/30 morning to resolve remaining open items and agree on DocuSign timeline.

Would 9:00 AM BST on 3/30 work for you for a 30-minute call?

Attachment: KM_comments_DPA.pdf (pdf, 78 KB)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 415 555 01xx

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines for MediSphere — suggested language and risks

Kim / Laura — I reviewed MediSphere_DPA_Redlines_v3 and KM_comments_DPA. Quick summary of the risk items I think we should flag back to the customer: 

1) Transfer impact / SCCs: MediSphere's proposed change to delete our existing SCC supplement introduces ambiguity around who runs the TIA and who retains the record of the assessment. Recommendation: keep Redwood's SCC supplement, add a short paragraph accepting joint TIA where customer supplies the business context and we provide technical mitigations.

2) Processor liability cap tweaks in section 12: their redline expands indemnity for third-party data processors — push back and propose a carveout for breaches caused by customer-provided data or instructions.

3) Subprocessor notification / approval: agree to 30-day notice but keep an approval-by-exception model for certain infra providers.

Proposed counter language (high level bullets to send to MediSphere):
- Insert a TIA addendum template as an exhibit (short, operational).
- Maintain Redwood's SCC text; allow customer to add specific data categories and processors as schedule.
- Keep liability cap but add explicit exclusions for data provided by customer that violates law or for willful misconduct.

I'll draft tracked changes for the DPA this morning and include the exhibit template. I also recommend we surface the hosting-region impact to Engineering — if they require EU-only residency for certain datasets, we'll need a scoped hosting SLA.

On the call 3/30 we should have: engineering rep, contracts + legal, and MediSphere legal.

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-03-29T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines for MediSphere — point-by-point and action plan

Julia — thanks for the redlines. Attached is a short action plan workbook (MediSphere_ActionPlan.xlsx) that breaks out each clause, Redwood's proposed response, owner, and target date. Summary of our positions:

- SCCs / TIA: We are open to a joint TIA workflow. Redwood will host the template (exhibit) and commit to providing the technical mitigation descriptions and evidence; MediSphere should supply the business context and intended export pathways. Target: complete draft TIA exhibit by 3/30 COB.
- Hosting residency: If MediSphere insists on EU-only production hosting, we will require an operational scope change and an addendum to the Order Form (pricing and schedule impact). We propose a phased approach — confirm critical datasets for EU-only now, finalize scope by 4/6.
- Liability and indemnities: Redwood accepts standard carveouts but cannot accept uncapped indemnities for broad processor actions. We propose tightened language that addresses customer-caused incidents.
- Subprocessor notifications: Agree to 30-day notice for non-security changes; 14-day for security-impacting providers.

Action items I assigned in the workbook:
- Kimberly: consolidate counter-redline and circulate (owner; due 3/29 EOD).
- Ben: prepare TIA exhibit draft and risk memo (owner; due 3/29 EOD).
- Julia / MediSphere: confirm hosting residency preference and share any internal policy docs that require EU-only controls (owner; due 3/30 morning).

Can we do a quick 30-minute alignment call 9:00 AM BST on 3/30? Please confirm — I've penciled it in on my side.

Attachment: MediSphere_ActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24 KB)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 650 555 03xx

Subject: Re: Draft DPA redlines for MediSphere — next steps and DocuSign

Kim / Laura / Ben — thanks for the clear plan and quick turnaround. We reviewed internally and are comfortable with the joint TIA approach and the proposed notice windows. A couple of clarifications:

- We'll send an internal memo this afternoon confirming the dataset list that must remain EU-only. Expect that by EOD 3/31.
- We accept the proposed TIA exhibit template in principle; please send the draft for review.

I've attached an updated redline (MediSphere_DPA_Redlines_v4.docx) with a few cleanups related to liability formatting and a short cover note. Once we get your consolidated counter-redline, I'm happy to proceed to DocuSign — please share the link when you're ready.
